questions.a: Restaurant SEO is the work of making your restaurant show up when someone nearby searches for the kind of food or experience you offer. It covers your Google Business Profile, your reviews, your website and the sites that link to you. Done well, it brings more foot traffic, phone calls and reservations from the neighborhoods you serve.

questions.q: How do I get my restaurant into the Google map pack?
questions.a: Start with a complete, accurate Google Business Profile: a clear description, consistent name, address and phone number, the right categories, good photos and up-to-date hours. Then keep a steady flow of reviews coming in and reply to them, since Google looks at review quality, quantity and recency. Location pages on your website and local backlinks help you compete too.

questions.q: Do review replies help my restaurant's local SEO?
questions.a: Yes, Google has confirmed that replying to reviews helps strengthen your local presence. Momos looked at two enterprise restaurant chains over several years and saw higher star ratings where reply rates were higher. Keep replies short, polite and specific to what the guest said, and skip promotions in your responses.

questions.q: Does each restaurant location need its own web page?
questions.a: If you run more than one location, you'll rank better with a dedicated page for each one. Google's local algorithm rewards pages that show real relevance to a specific area, and a single homepage can't do that for every city. Link each Google Business Profile to its own location page and make the content on each page unique.

questions.q: How do I get local backlinks for my restaurant?
questions.a: The best backlinks come naturally from your local community, so avoid buying them. List your restaurant in free local directories, pitch a story to food bloggers and critics, and take part in charity events, festivals or cooking demos that local media like to cover. When they write about you, they'll usually link to your website.

questions.q: How can I tell if my restaurant SEO is working?
questions.a: Your Google Business Profile dashboard is a good place to start, because it shows how often your listing appears in Search and Maps and what people do next. Rank-tracking tools can also map where you show up for a keyword across your area. Check these regularly so you can see which changes move your visibility.
